name: Madrid
summary: Build Madrid around its three art museums and long, late meals. Mornings for the Prado or palace, afternoons in Retiro, evenings moving between tapas bars.
seasonNote: July and August are very hot and many family restaurants close in August.
arrival: Metro line 8, the airport express bus and Cercanías trains all reach the centre in 30 to 40 minutes.
gettingAround: The centre is walkable and the metro covers the rest. Dinner starts after 9 pm.
cashTip: Cards are accepted nearly everywhere, including most bars.
foodTip: Have a bocadillo de calamares, tortilla, jamón ibérico and churros with thick chocolate.
buyTip: Espadrilles, saffron, good olive oil and vacuum-packed jamón (check customs rules for meat).
baseArea: Sol, Barrio de las Letras or Malasaña

connections.note: High-speed AVE, Iryo and Ouigo trains from Atocha; book ahead.
Air time only; add airport transfers.

items.name: Prado Museum
items.summary: Spain's national art museum: Velázquez, Goya, El Greco and Bosch.
items.expect: A huge collection; without a plan the visit becomes tiring.
items.tip: Book a timed ticket and pick 15 works; the last two hours are free but crowded.

whyVisit: Spain's national art museum: Velázquez, Goya, El Greco and Bosch.
Las Meninas, Goya's Black Paintings and The Garden of Earthly Delights are all here.
visitFlow: Start with Velázquez on the first floor.
Finish with Goya's Black Paintings.

items.name: Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum
items.summary: A private collection filling the gaps between the Prado and the Reina Sofía, from Italian primitives to Impressionists and Pop Art.
items.expect: Easier to see in a morning than the Prado; free on Monday afternoons for the permanent collection.
items.tip: Start on the top floor and work down chronologically.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.
items.sourceNote: Editorial selection. Durations, spending allowances and itinerary advice are planning estimates; check opening days and prices with the venue before you go.
whyVisit: A private collection filling the gaps between the Prado and the Reina Sofía, from Italian primitives to Impressionists and Pop Art.
Together with the Prado and Reina Sofía it forms Madrid's 'Golden Triangle of Art'.
visitFlow: Take the lift to the second floor for early European art.
Work down through Dutch and Impressionist rooms.
Finish with 20th-century art on the ground floor.
items.bestFor: Art lovers wanting breadth in one visit
tradeoffs: Easier to see in a morning than the Prado; free on Monday afternoons for the permanent collection.

items.name: Temple of Debod
items.summary: A 2nd-century BC Egyptian temple rebuilt on a hilltop park, given to Spain for helping save Nubian monuments from the Aswan Dam.
items.expect: The small interior has limited entry; the park around it is free and busy at sunset.
items.tip: Come for sunset over the Casa de Campo, then walk down to the Royal Palace.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.

whyVisit: A 2nd-century BC Egyptian temple rebuilt on a hilltop park, given to Spain for helping save Nubian monuments from the Aswan Dam.

visitFlow: Walk up through the Parque del Oeste.
See the temple reflected in its pool.
